title: gpu-oom-debug-notes-noah-evans
text:
Context:
- Repro intermittently on dedicated GPU nodes when running multi-stream batched inference with seq_len ~2048. Seen both during load testing and in canary deployments.
- Affected infra: p4d.24xlarge equivalent nodes (NVIDIA A100 80GB stack).
- Symptoms: immediate OOM on first allocation in some containers; in others, "cuda runtime error (2) : out of memory at ..." or driver mismatch messages.

Commands tried / quick checks:
1) Check GPU / driver on host
- nvidia-smi
  Thu Feb 20 12:03:21 2026
  +-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
  | NVIDIA-SMI 535.54.03    Driver Version: 535.54.03    CUDA Version: 12.1     |
  +-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+

- nvcc --version
  nvcc: NVIDIA (R) Cuda compiler driver
  Cuda compilation tools, release 12.1, V12.1.226

2) Inside container (image: redwood/serve:py3.11-cu118)
- python -c "import torch; print(torch.__version__, torch.version.cuda, torch.cuda.is_available())"
  2.2.1  11.8  True

- python -c "import ctypes; print(ctypes.CDLL('libcuda.so').cudaDriverGetVersion())"
  OSError: libcuda.so: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory

- ldd $(python -c 'import torch; import os; print(os.path.dirname(torch.__file__))')/lib/libtorch.so | grep cuda
  libcuda.so.1 => /usr/local/cuda-11.8/targets/x86_64-linux/lib/libcuda.so.1 (0x00007f4a3b6a0000)

Notes: Host has driver 535 (CUDA 12.1) but container expects CUDA 11.8 libs (image tags cu118). We mount /usr/local/cuda-11.8 from host to container via symlink in some nodes but not reliably across fleet.

Observed error snippets from logs (stack traces collapsed):
- RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 256.00 MiB (GPU 0; 79.00 GiB total capacity; 76.63 GiB already allocated; 2.87 GiB free; 77.50 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)
- torch.cuda.CudaError: CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version
- gstc: cuda driver mismatch: libcuda 535 != runtime 515 -> symbol lookup error: /opt/conda/lib/python3.11/site-packages/torch/lib/libtorch_cuda.so: undefined symbol: _ZN3c105...
- RuntimeError: cudaStreamSynchronize(nullptr) returned error 700 (Illegal address)

Hypotheses / likely causes:
- Mixed driver/runtime versions: host driver (535) vs container runtime (11.8) vs PyTorch built against 11.8/11.7. Some nodes have a different /usr/local/cuda symlink leading to libcuda mismatch.
- Binary incompatibility for some ops / kernels leading to illegal memory access which manifests as OOM or illegal address.
- Host-level GPU memory reservation by other processes (NVIDIA MIG or kubelet) causing lower visible free memory; our allocator + caching interacts poorly.
- NCCL / cuDNN incompatible versions causing crashes during collective operations in multi-stream workloads.

Actions taken (chronological):
- 2025-11-09: Reproduced on dev node; ran nvidia-container-cli to check devices accessible inside container -> OK.
- 2025-11-09: Switched image to redwood/serve:py3.11-cu121 (CUDA 12.1 build of PyTorch 2.2.1) on one canary host; errors disappeared for 48h.
- 2025-11-11: Rolled canary back to cu118 to test long-tail; issues reappeared -> correlates with runtime/driver mismatch hypothesis.
- 2025-11-12: Added LD_LIBRARY_PATH explicit bindmount to /usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64 -> mitigated libcuda not found but introduced symbol lookup errors in some containers.
- 2025-11-15: Captured strace of python process; failing syscalls show mmap failure followed by segfault in libtorch_cuda.so.

Commands that gave helpful info:
- docker run --rm --gpus all --env LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda-11.8/lib64 nvidia/cuda:11.8-base nvidia-smi
  (used to validate container-level visibility)
- python -c "import torch; print(torch.version.cuda, torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).total_memory)"
- grep -i cuda /var/log/syslog | tail -n 200
- ldd on libtorch_cuda.so to find which libcuda it's linking to
- /usr/bin/nvidia-container-cli -k list -> shows devices but also reported "error: driver mismatch" on two nodes (see INF-4123)

Temporary mitigations in cluster:
- Pin inference image to cu121 builds for fleet nodes that have driver >= 535. This reduced incidents by ~90% during spike.
- For nodes that must run cu118 images (legacy customers), use nodeSelector and taints to isolate to nodes with driver 515 that match runtime.
- Added kubelet eviction margin for GPU memory accounting to reduce chance that two large allocators fight for memory.

Permanent fixes under consideration:
- Standardize on container images built against CUDA 12.x for new PyTorch builds and phase out cu118 variants. Requires validation for customer-facing VMs.
- Improve startup checks in runtime: on container start, compare host nvidia-smi driver version to torch.version.cuda and log clear warnings + fail early if incompatible.
- Add a preflight that verifies libcuda.so version symlink inside container matches host driver (parse nvidia-smi driver version).
- Publish a KB article for SREs: "Driver/runtime mismatch diagnostics and quick fixes" with exact commands and remediation steps.

Unresolved questions / TODOs:
- Why did some containers report libcuda.so missing even though host provides it via driver 535? (Possibly container seccomp / chroot path differences) -> Need to check mount namespaces and container runtime version.
- Confirm whether pytorch caching behavior (reserved in total by PyTorch) can be tuned to avoid early OOM under high multiplexing. Try setting TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:64
- Investigate whether upgrading NCCL to match CUDA 12.x will be safe across all customer workloads.

Notes for next steps (short checklist):
- [ ] Add early-exit preflight script to serving runtime image (check driver vs runtime). (Owner: Raja)
- [ ] Run controlled A/B test of cu121 vs cu118 images under synthetic load for 7 days. (Owner: Asha)
- [ ] Update node provisioning scripts to record driver versions in node labels. (Owner: infra-team)
- [ ] Draft KB article and internal runbook. (Owner: me / Noah)

Relevant log excerpts (sanitized):
- E 2025-11-09 10:22:13 ServingRuntime.cpp:312 - cuda runtime error (2) : out of memory at /opt/conda/conda-bld/pytorch_1603247645336/work/aten/src/THC/THCGeneral.cpp:200
- E 2026-02-16 03:11:02 WorkerPool.cpp:88 - Caught CudaError: CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version -> restarting worker

References / notes:
- INF-4123 (internal ticket) logs node-level nvidia-container-cli failures for 3 nodes (attached).
- PR 678 updated serving Dockerfiles to include simple preflight for cuda driver.

If I get time: run a minimized repro that toggles LD_LIBRARY_PATH and mounts /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 into the container to see which combination reproduces symbol lookup vs OOM.

Contact: ping me on Slack @noah.evans or add notes on INF-4123.

End of notes.
